name: Rating
purpose: Lets a user express or view a star-based score. Itinerary row 25 (P3, 'Star / score input'). Two variants: an INPUT (a real fieldset of native radios) for the user to SET a rating, and a passive READ-ONLY DISPLAY for showing an aggregate score (e.g. '4.3 out of 5' on a product/review card) — the itinerary's own name spans both senses ('input') and the read-only case has no other gated home.
$status: PROPOSED #209, Dave's eye owed — new component, built through the gated-component route at #209 wave 3 lane B. Nothing about it is ruled.

props.name: value
props.$note: 1–5 whole stars in the input variant (native radiogroup, one value per star). The read-only display specimen shows a FRACTIONAL value (4.3) via a clip-path overlay — half/third-star granularity in the INPUT itself was not built; see $decisionsForDave.

props.name: readOnly
props.$note: true selects the passive display variant (role="img", the number in the accessible name, no interactive radios).

props.name: reviewCount
props.$note: Read-only variant only — the '(212 reviews)' trailing caption. Optional; the star value and number stand alone without it.

variants.name: input
variants.use: A real fieldset of 5 native radio buttons the user can set — 'Rate this product'.

variants.name: readOnly
variants.use: A passive aggregate score, e.g. on a product or review card.

tokens.star-filled: text/default — the same ink checkbox/radio already use, NOT an invented gold/amber (see $decisionsForDave)
tokens.star-empty: form/border/default — the same outline token Selection-controls' checkbox border binds
tokens.label: text/default @ .t-cm-label (fieldset legend) / .t-cm-caption (the '3 out of 5' live value text) / .t-cm-figure-6 (the read-only numeric score) / .t-cm-caption (review count)
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. Every value already exists and is already bound by Selection-controls' checkbox/radio.

motion.hover: Filled colour previews on hover before commit (:hover ~ label, CSS-only), reduced-motion collapses only the colour transition, not the state.

responsive.rule: Inline-flex star row; wraps naturally inside any container width down to a single star's own 32px hit target. No breakpoint-specific behaviour needed.

accessibility.role: Input variant: a real <fieldset>/<legend> containing role="radiogroup" (implicit, via 5 grouped native <input type="radio">) — the SAME native-keyboard idiom Selection-controls already earns honestly for grouped Radio ('native checkbox/radio/switch have NO JS keyboard model by design'), copied rather than hand-rolled. Read-only variant: role="img" with the full sentence ('Rated 4.3 out of 5') as its accessible name; the star row itself is aria-hidden.
accessibility.keyboard: Native radio keyboard model (Arrow keys move selection, Tab enters/exits the group) — zero custom JS keydown, same as Selection-controls' plain Radio (not its chip radiogroup, which needed custom roving-tabindex because chips are <button>s; native <input type=radio> does not).
accessibility.liveValue: An aria-live="polite" caption ('3 out of 5') updates on change so a screen-reader user hears the committed value, not just 'radio button 3 of 5, checked'.
accessibility.colourIndependence: The filled/empty distinction is never the only carrier: the input variant always shows the live text value; the read-only variant's accessible name carries the number directly, independent of the visual clip. 1.4.1 is satisfied by TEXT, not by star count alone.
accessibility.targetArea: Each star's label is a 32px box (24px glyph inside), short of the 44px floor — DECLARED, not silent: five 44px targets in a row would force 220px minimum width, which the itinerary's inline-with-label placements (product cards, review rows) do not have room for. Flagged as a NAMED open question, not resolved by shrinking the floor silently.

antiPatterns: Building the star fill with a custom keydown handler instead of native radio inputs — no honest AT signal is gained by doing so, and Selection-controls' own reasoning for staying native applies unchanged
Conveying the rating by colour or star-fill alone with no text value nearby (1.4.1)

Inventing a half-star glyph for the INPUT variant instead of either committing to a coarser step or building a proper half-star hit-target model — this pass deliberately stopped at whole stars for the input and left fractional values to the read-only display only
Reusing this component's read-only variant as a review WRITE form disguised as a display — the input variant exists precisely so an input never masquerades as role="img"

tokenValidation.result: PROPOSED — worker lane B build, #209. No gate has been run by this worker (conductor's serial set runs _validate_snippets.py / _validate_a11y.py / _validate_type_composites.py / _validate_radius.py / _validate_icons.py / _validate_coverage.py). This is a proposal, not a proof-of-done.
tokenValidation.$note: The star glyph path is byte-matched from knowledge/assets/icons/global-controls/favourite-star.svg (a real library asset, not invented), referenced via <symbol>/<use> with an explicit fill="currentColor" on the <path> so the CSS `color` property (not `fill`) controls the empty/filled/hover states — <use> shadow-tree content does not match ordinary `svg path` descendant selectors from outside, which was caught and fixed by an actual render (see receipt).

provenance.$note: Itinerary row 25 (reviews/ITINERARY-STATUS-2026-08-19-v1.json), measured a TRUE GAP: all five signal probes negative, no plausible store alias, drift AGREES.

$differsFrom.Selection-controls (Radio): Radio selects ONE option from a labelled set of alternatives with equal semantic weight; Rating's five radios are not alternatives — they are an ORDINAL scale where selecting '3' implies stars 1–2 are also 'included'. The visual fill expresses that ordinality; a plain Radio group never does.
$differsFrom.Chips (single-selection, Selection-contr: The chip radiogroup is custom (role=radiogroup on <button>s with hand-rolled roving Arrow/Home/End) because chips are not native form controls. Rating's radiogroup uses REAL <input type=radio>, so no custom keydown was needed — a simpler case, not a re-implementation of the chip pattern.

$decisionsForDave: Should the filled star use a warm/gold tint (a new token) rather than mono ink? The store has no such seat today and 'no token minting' is on this wave's DO-NOT-RULE list, so mono ink was used deliberately, not by oversight.
Is a whole-star-only input acceptable, or is half-star precision needed? If so, the hit-target/keyboard model needs a fresh design (this pass did not attempt it).
The 32px (not 44px) per-star target: accept for compact/inline placements, or should Rating carry a distinct 'roomy' variant with true 44px targets for a standalone rating page?
